findings.title: Debug logging uses log.Error level
findings.body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags use r.log.Error(...) for routine informational logging of counts (e.g. 'Annotations to clean by time', 'cleaned annotations by time'). This is not an error condition and will pollute error logs/alerting on every cleanup cycle. Should be Debug or Info level.

findings.title: deleteByIDs loses non-SQLite batch deadlock protection by not splitting large ID lists
findings.body: deleteByIDs builds a single DELETE ... WHERE id IN (...) statement with up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize parameters for non-SQLite databases. For large batch sizes this still issues one large multi-row DELETE statement which can hold locks for an extended period, partially re-introducing the kind of lock contention this PR is trying to avoid, since the fix only addressed the subquery lock scope, not statement size for MySQL under large batch configs.

findings.title: Fetch and delete occur in separate non-transactional statements, allowing race / double counting
findings.body: fetchIDs and deleteByIDs are now executed as two separate WithDbSession calls without a shared transaction. Between the SELECT and subsequent DELETE, rows matching the condition could be concurrently modified (e.g. tags change, or org cleanup settings elsewhere), causing deletes of IDs that no longer meet the criteria, or missing newly matching rows. The PR documents accepting under-deletion but doesn't address potential over-deletion by ID when a row's content changed between fetch and delete (e.g. an annotation unexpectedly becoming non-matching no longer matters because deletion is by ID only, so any row with that ID gets deleted regardless of current state).

findings.title: Cleanup job interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute without justification
findings.body: The ticker interval for running all cleanup jobs (including unrelated ones like snapshot/dashboard version/image/query history cleanup) was reduced from every 10 minutes to every 1 minute. This is a 10x increase in frequency for all cleanup jobs, not just annotation cleanup, which could increase load unnecessarily and isn't explained in the PR description, which only discusses deadlock avoidance via query splitting.
